sense.text:
“For gold is tried in the fire.” Forged by fire is the trials and tribulations we go through that purify us, that clean out the wickedness we have inside of us. It is not just something burning: it is something being purged, being tried, being cleaned. Fire is a purifier, one of the best purifiers, and that is why the Most High uses fire all through the Bible to purify. It burns out the impurities, the bad elements, the things that are going to corrupt you. If he didn't use the fire, you wouldn't get cleaned. You need those trials.

The people who deal with the metals heat them up to burn out the impurities, because to get the best element the impurities have to be burned out. That is us: to get the best you, the impurities have to burn out. We are not just in the fire, we are being turned into something, like the gold poured out of the forge. Something is being burned out of us to turn us into the next element.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” That is the qualifier. When you come to serve the Lord and sign up to do the Lord's work, now you are in the furnace. Now the Lord can deal with you, and now the fire turns on.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure”, because the fire never turns off. The impurities never stop, so the fire never stops. You are constantly bombarded, constantly pressured to do the wrong thing. Look at social media, look at the world being turned upside down; the heathen is raging. Everything that's wrong in the earth is because the damn heathen is over us: the people over the earth right now are wicked. So there is no rest. If you find yourself at rest, you are not being purged. The fire is not on you, you're off the stove, you're cold. Matter of fact, you're in the refrigerator.

“And make not haste in time of trouble”, because that fire has to stay on you to burn the impurities out. Get off the stove and you cool down, the impurities stop burning out of you, and you go back to the state you were in. Make haste and leave this, and who turns the fire back on? The Most High God turned the fire on you in the beginning and he is the one who keeps it on you. Turn your back to him, and nobody turns it back on.

Satan makes it easy for you. He gives you your heart's desire: the lady next door, the coworker, the porn, here's your whole algorithm. The fire is the restraint: putting the phone down, putting blocks on your phone, throwing the damn phone in the trash if it got too bad for you. The fire is the restraint, turning away from evil.

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.” To be increased at your last end is getting the kingdom. It is not hard to be understood. We are doing this for a reason: the fire has a reason and the restraint has a reason. You have to go through this to get to the next level.

If you are not fighting, you are relaxing, and relaxing gets you nowhere. There is no sitting still and no neutral, only forward or reverse. Either you are on the right, hot and fervent for this truth, or on the left and ice cold. Christ said pick one. If you're in the middle, you're going to die.

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully.” Whatever trial comes, take it cheerfully, because the trials have to come to purge it out of you. The fire has to stay on you. It is not going to get easy, and it is not supposed to be easy. Stub your toe in the night and say, Lord, take away the pain; but don't say, Lord, I give up. Don't be stupid.

Your family turns against you, you lose your job: do you give up ten, fifteen years in the truth to go back to your damn stupid family, eat the ham sandwich and open the Christmas gifts so they welcome you back with open arms? Do you turn your back on the brothers and sisters that labored in this truth with you? After all you suffered and endured, when you get there, absolutely nothing is waiting for you. Putting the ball down is easy. Continuing to labor with your brother is the hard part, and that is unity: knowing my brother is going through it the same way I am, and leaning on each other. That's why we are supposed to be Malachi 3:16: give me a call, I know you lost your job, are you good, is your family good, if you need something let me know. Walk ten years together and act like you don't know your brother when he is going through something, and you are the damn devil the Bible speaks of.

Leave your men on the battlefield and say, good luck, I hope it works out for y'all, and in the military you get shot for that. They declare you a deserter and take you round back, because that is what you deserve. Leave your people on the field and you are saying, I hope you die too. And this is not our first go round together: if you left us this time, how many other times have you left us?

“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.” That is what it is supposed to do. We are supposed to go through this, and as we go through it we grow in the spirit. Work out and the muscle breaks down and grows bigger; never work out and your muscles never grow. Never read and you never learn how to read. The more you go through trials and tribulations, the stronger you get at going through them: one trial, then the next, and you are stronger for each.

Never go through anything, and the first trial trips you up and throws you out. That's why some brothers bug the hell out at the first trial: they never been through nothing. That's why leadership says, how can I trust you if I've never seen you go through anything? Fresh on the battlefield, your temperament has to be seen. Will you go right or left when you go through it? Will you betray me the first chance you get, give me up for the least thing when the pressure comes around the corner?

“But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.” Patience perfects it. God does not want to destroy you with your trials; he wants to build you with your trials. He is perfecting you and making you stronger with each one, and each trial takes you up to the next level. It's levels to this thing. Some are in kindergarten because they never been through nothing. As you grow your spirit grows, and you become strong enough to endure the next level. But if you never been through nothing, how can the Lord trust you?

Brothers peeled out at the first sign of trouble, and for nonsense: I got so much on my plate, it's too much, I'll do the same thing but on my own terms. If you would leave for that, what would the real trial bring? Everybody got an excuse.

“The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts.” All these vessels are used for different reasons, but the Lord tries your heart and your mind. He sees what you're really about; all the other things are superficial. How are you really going to deal with issues and problems, with each other, with your wife, your kids, the congregation? Some brothers can't deal with anything, not even themselves, so how are they going to deal with the next man, or the sisters? When your kids are in here acting a fool, we know how your house looks.

It is spiritual. You think you're hiding it, but you're not hiding it at all. This is the furnace: the Lord puts you in it to see how you are going to deal with the matter.

We go through it together, push and endure a little at a time. Some things are easier for one than another, but it balances out: work together and it is easier for us, and we bear each other's burdens. If you are a one-man team, I guess you don't need us.

“Every man’s work shall be made manifest”: it is going to be revealed. “For the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire”: by trials. Nobody is going to pour lighter fluid on you. Your trials are what reveal you; as your trials come, that's where you get your grades. How you deal with the matter, how strong you are in the spirit, is revealed. You lose your job and bug the hell out, your wife loses her job and you throw yourself out the window. Is this the first time you ever seen poverty? We thrive in poverty; we became a nation under slavery. You think it's all about you, a one-man nation: you got in an accident, so you drink yourself to sleep. Every single one of us has trials and tribulations.

“And the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is.” The Lord has them custom made for you, to try you and your spirit and see what you are made of. Your trial is not my trial. What comes easy for you might never come easy for me, and what comes easy for me might never come easy for you. That's the way the Lord made it. But we are all joined together, each with skill sets unique to us: the officer who speaks Spanish goes out, and the brother who can only pass out flyers goes on the mission with him and helps, because we are going to do the Lord's work.

“If any man’s work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man’s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.” That fire is going to burn up that work, but that man is going to be saved.

A leader went through something, and others bugged out, but he stayed in the fight: the trial was for everyone, but he continued on while others fell to the wayside. It's about endurance, enduring to the end. It might not be pretty, you might get scuffed up, but keep pushing. The Lord is not trying to kill you; he wants to see what you are made of.

“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. There is an escape route for everybody. He is not going to put more on you than you can endure. He doesn't give the alcoholic the alcohol; you walk into the bar and buy it. The whoremonger puts himself in that situation. He tries you, but he doesn't tempt you: you tempt yourself. You can't play the stupid word games with God and say, God, you tempted me, God did this to me. You did that to yourself, and you are going to pay. Leave your men on the battlefield and say God put us in this situation, and you are going to pay for that.

“But will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. Going through trials and tribulations, all you got to do is pick up the phone: my brother, I'm going through it. Go to leadership: I got this going on. But your pride won't let you. It all boils down to sin. Why can't you fix your family? Sin. Why is your wife out of control, your kids out of control? Sin. Still dealing with porn? Sin. You won't fix your problem because you're infatuated with sin. You won't let go of the tail of that snake until it bites you and puts you to death. It's you. It's not God.

“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” We got to go through this and suffer, because we deserve it and we got to get fixed. We got to walk through this fire. To get to heaven you got to walk through hell, and if you don't want to get fixed, you stay in hell. As we grow, it gets easier to move to the next level, and at the next level more trials and tribulations are waiting. Don't give up because there are trials there.

You train your mind to know it when you see it: this is a trial for me to work through. I make a covenant with my eyes; my algorithm is starting to look crazy, I need to stop clicking on that and stay off social media. It is not going to stop. They put it on YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, the commercials, the t-shirt section in the store, because it is a trial in you that you have to deal with, at different levels.

“What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?” The Most High is trying to make it right for us, giving us ways out of these problems. He will never put you in a situation where you can't call your brother and fix it. Offend your brother joking around, and he has to make the phone call and make it right; if he doesn't, it falls on him.

Not the call the day before the Day of Atonement, if I have offended you in the slightest bit over the past two years: that's not authentic, and you don't mean it. In the moment: that hurt. My fault, we good. Problem solved, right then and there. Carry it for years and it becomes a part of you, and no apology fixes it. That is how black people do, not our righteous people. We have to be a righteous people again. These trials and tribulations are geared toward fixing us. Keep doing it the same way and expect it to change, and that's insanity. We have to change as a people, start moving in the right direction, and let the Lord take the rest.

“He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?” The Most High is trying to give us a kingdom. Christ went through the furnace, and he is doing the same thing with us. We are the ambassadors of Christ: do you think you are not going to go through the same thing, that you are not going to be punished? Yes, you are.

“Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?” It doesn't say what; it says who: a person. Anybody or anything you put in front of Christ becomes your idol, to include yourself, your mama, your sister, your baby. Christ came to bring division: put your mother, your father, your sister or your brother before him and you are not worthy of this truth or of the kingdom, because you allowed a person to come between you and the Lord.

“Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?” Then it names the things that can separate you: your trials, distress, troubles, and persecution. You will be persecuted for this truth; it's coming. Look at Karmelo Anthony, the brother who stabbed the Edomite: how he could be framed and go to jail for thirty-five years. Social media can persecute you now: AI can show you a video of yourself doing something until you doubt yourself, and your own people will say, I didn't think he would do that, and testify against you. Technology is putting us right where the scripture says it will. We read this thinking it is far off, but it is not. The persecution is already here; being put on trial and put to death for this truth is already here. If you give up or turn your back on this truth because of the trials and tribulations, shame on you.

“For thy sake we are killed all the day long”: for whose sake? For Christ's sake. “We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.”

“Nor things present, nor things to come”: the things that are now and the things to come. “Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” And there is a period at the end of that. Nothing should be able to separate you, because you know what is at the end and that it is waiting on us: paradise is waiting on us at the end of this.

Everything you are going to go through is for a reason. You are going to be persecuted, lied on, and your family is going to turn their back on you; if it has not happened, it will happen. But don't give up. You are being put in a furnace to be tried and turned into pure gold. Your wicked family turning their back on you? Good. Coming into the truth gets rid of a whole lot of dead weight and useless conversations about sports and holidays. If it ain't about the scriptures, don't talk to me, because that is what's beneficial for me and for you.

precepts.why:
“For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you. Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord”. We are going to go through the same thing. “Neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him. If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.”

Christ was the example, and we are the example. We are going to walk in the same footsteps and get punished the same way. It is not going to be easy, and it is not supposed to be easy. If our Lord and Master went through it, do you not think you are going to go through it, that you deserve to go through it?

So when God spared not his own Son but delivered him up for us all, it shows the road to the kingdom he is freely giving: Christ went through the furnace first, and the servant is not greater than his lord.

sense.text:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth”. Why would he correct us, rebuke us and take us through this if he didn't love us? The correction comes because of the love, not the opposite. Otherwise he would cut us off: look at Esau, he cut him off because he hates him.

Some of you say, man, I'm going through it. You're supposed to go through it. Three flat tires? So what: you got one more than you deserve. We all go through it, but we keep pushing, because at the end of the day a whole kingdom is waiting on us. The world being turned right side up is waiting on us; even the animals are waiting on us. The whole world is waiting for us to stand up, and we have to do it manfully, the right way. We can't skate by. We do it together or we don't do it at all. “And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.”

“If ye endure chastening”: it says if. “God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” As a father you have to correct your son; if you don't correct him, you don't love him. A father wants to see his son do better than him, and if you don't want that, you don't love him as a son. In the truth, the leaders are fathers over the congregation, heads of the school, and want to see every man in here do better than them. Their leadership are fathers over them, and they get chastised as much as you do, if not more. That is out of love. But you turn your back to that and want to take your ball and go home. The hell with you then.

precepts.why:
Going back to the fire: that correction, that chastisement, is the Lord trying your heart, seeing what your heart is made of. “The furnace proveth the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.” The furnace proves the potter's vessel, and what the Lord proves is man's reasoning. When the Lord turns up the heat on your behind, he tries your heart.

A couple flat tires, you lose a job, and now you want to pick up a job on the Sabbath: your reasoning is off, and now it is revealed. Covetous: you can't deal with your lowest state. You get checked, and maybe it wasn't exactly your fault, but you don't take the low; you argue, you have strife. That's ego, and it revealed your thoughts.

When the metal is melted, every metal has its own temperature to melt and be purged. So as the fire goes up in your life, different spirits come out and rise to the top. He is trying your reasoning: are you going to deal with it or not? He is dealing with you as a son: are you going to respect him as a father? That is why Ecclesiasticus 2 says to take whatever is brought upon you cheerfully: you are getting purged as he tries your reasoning, and you show forth your understanding, whether you are actually learning and applying everything you have been hearing.

sense.text:
Even when you are getting tried, there is another element the Lord is showing you. A lot of brothers and sisters like to suffer in silence, so the Lord is not only trying you but showing you that your communication is weak and you need to grow in that area. The Lord is giving us lifelines, and we have to use them.

“Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another”. When you are going through things you lean on the brothers: pick up the phone, Captain, Officer, I'm struggling in this area. But because of pride we suffer in silence, and then you start to be offended with everybody around you, they don't really like me, where's the charity, and you find yourself out the door. That's how brothers and sisters get down. Spake often: not only on the Sabbath. And when a brother asks how you doing and you say, I'm enduring, that was an opportunity right there.

And it is not really silence, because the spirit is seen on you. Are you okay, sister? I'm okay, while you look absolutely bugged out. There's nothing worse than seeing a brother pout. We all go through trials and tribulations, but we are here for each other. This is about unity.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” The Bible is about unity, not separation. We separate from the wicked, not the righteous. We join together to get over the hurdles and push through, because by unifying we are stronger: the fist is strong together, apes strong together. If we don't fight together, we are going to lose together.

When brothers don't take the opportunity for unity, they are saying they have no hope in the people around them; they have no hope in anything, and hope everything fails. That one is the spot in the feast. When we come to the unity of the faith we are able to purge those things out of the body, but the spot holds that sin in so tight that he would rather be a spot in the feast and destroy the unity of the body. He may be the reason things aren't moving in the body.

precepts.why:
“These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.” Against them: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life. And of some have compassion, making a difference: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.”

That flesh is the fleshy, sinful spirit, the sensual spirit that does not want to fix itself and does not want to do right. They don't want to be unified with everybody else and don't want to see this work succeed. They leave and hope everything else fails, because they don't want to succeed themselves. God does not deal in that manner. That's why it is more about building than separating.

Anytime you see anything about separation, it is about getting that one out of the body so the body can continue to grow. You can't have that sensual spirit and think you can grow inside the body. No: you go out of the body, and be without the body. That is the contrast with brethren dwelling together in unity.

sense.text:
“And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone. As I live, saith the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you: And I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered”. “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.” This is when we go back into the wilderness, in our deliverance from Babylon, and Christ deals with us and teaches us the laws again. And in one word, what he is doing to us there is purging us.

That is what this is all about. Even then it is still a time of purge. Even after the one third, there are still going to be bad actors among us, people who still need to get right, and they are going to get it. And who is going to give it to them? Christ.

“Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you, saith the Lord God.” What kind of pleading is he going to be doing? It's not baby, baby, please. It's not a damn R&B song. The pleading is killing, smiting.

“And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: And I will purge out from among you the rebels”. What kind of purge? Not the purge from the movie: killing. “And them that transgress against me: I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

precepts.why:
“For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh”. With all flesh.

That is the pleading of Ezekiel 20: not begging, but killing and smiting, by fire and by his sword. And when the Lord purges out the rebels from among us, that purge is the same: killing.

“I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there”. No baby, baby, please for them either. “For my people and for my heritage Israel”: for his people Israel, he will kill them.

Put next to Ezekiel 20, the same word plead shows what the Lord does to the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat, and what he will do with the rebels of Israel face to face in the wilderness.

“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” With an unquenchable fire. That is the purge of Ezekiel 20:38: the wheat gathered into the garner, and the rebels and them that transgress burned up like chaff. Does anybody not understand that?

sense.text:
“And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”. We are still talking about the purge. The Lord is not going to give the kingdom to wicked negroes; the kingdom will not be open to wicked negroes. To get the kingdom you have to go through this fire and get right. There is no other way. You can't keep doing what you do and think you're going to get the kingdom; it is impossible. That's why we got to fight for this and help each other.

If I see you weak and don't say nothing to you, that means I hate you. Tell a brother, you got to fix that, and he says, you hate me. Bro, shut your ass up, I'm trying to save your life. We are so used to not taking correction from each other that it feels like hate, because you've never been corrected. Everybody coddled you and nobody said anything, so you kept kicking the can down the street, no harm no foul, until you're back on the corner doing what you do.

“But the third shall be left therein.” The third are those the Most High is going to save, and even they still have to be sifted. Even out of the third, it still has to be refined, made right, purged.

You're going through stuff, and now you want to quit, and you ain't relying on the brotherhood. “In the day of prosperity”: when things are going well. “There is a forgetfulness of affliction”: you forget what it's like to be in a low estate, so you have to take heed lest you fall. “And in the day of affliction”: when the fire comes up and the heat gets turned up. “There is no more remembrance of prosperity.”

Remember, the trying of your faith worketh patience, and Ecclesiasticus 2 warns those who have lost patience. In adversity you forget the last end, the increase the Lord is going to give you, and the things he has in store. If you just purge your spirit you would be able to receive everything the Lord has promised in the future. But you quit because you forgot what the goal was, forgot the mission, and want to abandon ship. When you are going through adversity you have to be patient in your lowest state and not forget the prosperity to come. That is what strengthens your faith.

“And then shall many be offended”. In this purging process a lot of people are going to turn their back to the Lord. What people forget is that they are not turning their back to us. We are nothing but humble servants of the Lord doing the Lord's work, working together in the vineyard, so you are turning your back to the master and saying, I don't want to do the work no more. I'm not turning my back to the Lord, I'm turning my back to y'all? You got it mixed up, my brother.

“And shall betray one another”: when you turn your back to your brother, it is called betrayal. “And shall hate one another.”

“And many false prophets shall rise”. So you say, I can do the work outside of the body, I don't have to be here, I can do my own thing somewhere else. If you were going to do the work somewhere else, why wouldn't you do the work here and continue the mission? You had no intention of doing the work. “And shall deceive many”: they deceive the simple.
“And because iniquity shall abound”: the short word is sin. “The love of many shall wax cold.”

“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” As you fight till the end. That is the only way you are going to get salvation: you have to walk through hell to get to heaven. There is no shortcut to the kingdom and no roundabout; you got to walk straight through to get there. And if you don't want to do it, don't do it.

“And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” That is how you are going to get saved: as the Most High refines us and burns the iniquity out of us, as we get purged and go through the trials we have to overcome. There is no other way.

You got the fire on one side and the deep water on the other; the only way is the straight line. There are no shortcuts for black people. That's a hard thing to understand: you think you can take the short way there, but you can't. You got to take the long route. The Most High has to prove you to see if you are worthy of a kingdom.

“Blessed are they that do his commandments”. As we keep these commandments we are proving our worthiness and passing the grade, going from one grade to the next, one trial to the next, one temperament to the next. That is what God intended: we have to grow in this truth. Brothers have been in this truth ten, fifteen years, the Bishop almost thirty; you see the works and what it looks like to do the work. Do you think there is a shortcut, one, two, three years and that's it? Then you start your own thing with the Bishop's precept book, you damn idiot, a brand new fool with other fools following you, against leadership that has labored twenty plus years doing this work.

“That they may have right to the tree of life”: meaning you earned it. When he puts the crown on your head, you earned it. You fought to the end, did everything asked of you, accomplished everything put in front of you, went from grade to grade to grade. Job well done. You've been proven like fine gold; you passed the grade. Some brothers are junk metal, fool's gold: they just look shiny, the appearance of godliness.

“That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire”: with your trials. Your trials purify you and prove you. They make sure you're right, make sure you're not fool's gold, make sure you're pure. There is no other way. It's not a cakewalk, and it's not supposed to be.

The whole time we've been talking, it says the trial of your faith is valued more than gold, and not just more: much more. People die looking for gold, and what you are going to be is more than gold. “Might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ”. That's what we are looking for: Christ coming and saying, job well done, my faithful servant, and sealing us worthy of a kingdom. That is what we fight day and night for. I know you're tired, we all get tired, but don't give up. Once you step out, who's to say you can step back in? Once you get off the offramp, who's to say you got enough gas to get back on? Don't play games with God. Don't roll the dice with God.

If you want to hear God laugh, tell him your plan. Your plan is not God's plan. What God has planned for you is keep his commandments and live; everything else happens because of that. Nothing he put in your path is to destroy you. Everything adverse that happens to you is because you did it: your family is out of order because you're out of order, your wife is out of order because you're out of order, your kids are out of order because you and your wife are out of order. A backdoor marriage, and you are always going to have a problem, because you started out of order. You want your life to be easy? Keep God's commandments. There is no secret recipe to this thing.

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” Does it say anything after that about do what you want to do? No. Keep God's commandments and live: that's the secret recipe. That's what they hid from us, put on the shelf right over our head. The pastor says, do what I say do and it's going to be all right, and it hasn't worked out for us. It doesn't work that way. God's commandments are in this Bible, and we have to do what this Bible says.

“No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” You can't do what you want to do. You have to do it the right way: straight, straight up.

This is agriculture. You plow, then you sow, then you harvest, then you replenish, and plowing is the first step. When people stop doing the work, they get disenchanted with the things they did first. Don't get disenchanted with what you did when you first came in; go back to that first love, and hold your beginning confidence steadfast to the end. When you lose that first step, you can't do the rest that leads to the harvest.

So much of the Bible is agriculture, because that was our culture back then: we had our own, and we are going to get our own again. If you don't know how to self-sustain, learn it. Get the body together, unify, be communal, so those serious about the walk can be fed in that day. He has never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread; so when the grinding is low, as prophecy says, it is the local congregation's job to be self-sufficient for the people. That's what love is.

“I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.” That's what we all have to do. We all have to repent and get ourselves right, because at the end of the day it is to our benefit.
